title: Embedding & Rerank: Throttling buildup causing degraded throughput and score drift
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: A sudden buildup of queued reranking requests combined with a model variant upgrade caused sustained throughput drops (15-40% depending on cluster) and increased latency tail. Several enterprise customers experienced rerank timeouts and score inconsistencies compared to pre-upgrade behavior.
impact: Between 2025-11-10 02:40 UTC and 2025-11-10 05:20 UTC we observed a 23% average throughput reduction across embedding+ranks endpoints and P99 latency increase from 380ms to 1.1s. Four paying customers reported timeouts or degraded SLAs; overall request failure rate peaked at 4.7% in affected regions.
timeline: 2025-11-10 02:15 UTC - Autoscaler rollout for cluster pool-ryu started (config change ENG-12800)
2025-11-10 02:38 UTC - Spike in queued rerank requests observed; KV cache miss ratio increased by 62%
2025-11-10 02:46 UTC - First customer report of rerank timeouts (internal ticket CUST-438)
2025-11-10 03:05 UTC - On-call routed to serving runtime team; temporary rate limits applied to low-tier accounts
2025-11-10 03:22 UTC - Investigations show model-variant v2.7 push increased average decode length and memory pressure
2025-11-10 03:40 UTC - Rolled back model-variant v2.7 -> v2.6 for rerank pool (partial rollback) which reduced queue depth by ~35%
2025-11-10 04:10 UTC - Increased dedicated pool autoscaling max nodes by 25% as mitigant
2025-11-10 05:18 UTC - Metrics stabilized; P99 latency back down to ~420ms
2025-11-11 09:00 UTC - Post-incident review scheduled and internal notes published
root_cause: Multiple contributing factors: 1) A model variant (v2.7) deployed to rerank changed tokenization/sequence behavior increasing average KV cache working set, 2) an autoscaler config change reduced short-term burst capacity for the pool (concurrent with the deployment), and 3) a recently tightened per-customer soft throttle interacted poorly with increased per-request memory, causing queue buildup and eviction churn. None of the three alone would have produced the observed severity.
immediate_mitigations: Rollback model-variant v2.7 -> v2.6 for rerank traffic (completed 2025-11-10 03:40 UTC)
Temporarily raise autoscaler max nodes and reduce cooldown to absorb backlog
Relax per-customer soft throttle for enterprise tiers for 2 hours
Apply targeted KV cache retention tuning to reduce eviction churn
long_term_actions: (Owner: Diego Martinez) Add pre-deployment sequence-length and KV-cache footprint test to model onboarding pipeline - Due 2025-12-05
(Owner: Priya Sethi) Autoscaler policy audit and add a burst-capacity safety net for rerank pools - Due 2025-11-28
(Owner: Marcus Lee) Implement a live canary validator that runs a representative rerank workload during variant rollout (fail rollout on >5% queue increase) - Due 2025-12-12
(Owner: Elena Novak, Product) Re-evaluate soft throttle tiering thresholds and document customer SLA exceptions - Due 2025-11-30
(Owner: SRE) Add composite alert that correlates KV cache miss rate + queue depth + P99 latency to reduce mean time to detect - Due 2025-11-24
QA_and_validation: Add integration test that runs synthetic rerank traffic with elevated sequence lengths against new variants
Add nightly regression job comparing rerank score distributions (KS test) between current and candidate versions
Extend load testing to include KV cache stress scenarios (eviction-heavy workloads)
post_incident_notes: Decision: Prefer staged rollouts with a validator harness over broad variant pushes for rerank-sensitive pools; accepted slower rollout cadence as trade-off for stability
Trade-off: Implementing live canary validator adds ~15% deploy complexity but expected to avoid future customer-impacting regressions
Review feedback from PM and Design: better public documentation on expected score drift after model changes to set customer expectations
customer_communication: Notified affected customers via status page and targeted emails within 2 hours of detection. Follow-up summary and action plan shared the next business day with priority customers. No data loss; customers were offered credits proportional to downtime per SLA policy.
notes: This incident highlighted an operational blind spot where model-level memory characteristics were not part of our automated preflight checks. Adding KV-cache footprint checks and a canary validator are top priorities. Also capture lessons in runbook for on-call playbooks (queue+cache correlated failures).
